BERT4Rec’s bidirectional attention requires masked-item supervision: ordinary shifted next-item targets can remain visible elsewhere in the input. Deployment appends a reserved [MASK] token and scores its representation; the paper also includes last-item masking during training to match this task. Diagnostics must distinguish random interior reconstruction from prefix-only next-item prediction. [Original paper, §3.6](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690).

Practical probes inferred from this contract: trace each supervised position to its original target, verify its required masking, and detect shifted-target exposure by position/provenance rather than banning legitimate repeated item IDs. Compare diagnostic and deployed predictor logits on identical histories, truncation, position IDs, appended masks and candidates, with dropout disabled. For left-padded inputs, select the greatest nonpadding index—including the appended mask—never nonpadding-count minus one. Test short, full-length and empty histories; full-length histories must reserve room for the mask. Deliberately expose a shifted target, omit the appended mask, and substitute count-minus-one readout as positive controls: structural checks should flag each corruption, without requiring a predictable accuracy change. Verify bidirectional attention among valid tokens and padding exclusion. Check checkpoint-reloaded predictor scores against the trained model. Report sample counts, metric definitions and unavailable/NaN results when no eligible samples exist; missing evidence must not become a healthy zero. These are proposed engineering checks, not measured findings or a diagnostic suite prescribed by the paper.
